title: Was Stalin Necessary? Counterfactual Evidence on Soviet Growth
abstract: arXiv:2609.00418v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This article evaluates whether the exceptionally rapid growth of the Russian and Soviet economy after 1928 requires a specifically Stalinist explanation. The analysis treats this historical question as a sequence of increasingly demanding counterfactual comparisons rather than a binary comparison between observed growth and a single alternative. Long run output series from the Global Macro Database and the Maddison Project are combined with synthetic control, augmented synthetic control, synthetic difference in differences, interactive factor models, matrix completion, prediction benchmarks, historical analogues, spatial and temporal placebos, donor pool perturbations, endpoint sensitivity, and independent Soviet national account reconstructions. translated_title: 斯大林是必要的吗？关于苏联经济增长的反事实证据
translated_abstract: 本文评估了1928年后俄罗斯和苏联经济的异常快速增长是否需要一种特定的“斯大林主义”解释。该分析没有将这一历史问题简化为观察到的增长与单一替代方案之间的二元比较，而是将其处理为一系列要求逐步提高的反事实比较。研究将来自全球宏观经济数据库和麦迪逊项目的长期产出序列，与合成控制法、增强合成控制法、合成双重差分法、交互因子模型、矩阵补全、预测基准、历史类比、空间与时间安慰剂检验、捐赠池扰动、端点敏感性分析以及独立的苏联国民经济核算重建等多种方法相结合。本文的一个关键方法论贡献是构建了修正后的新经济政策反事实：该分析不再对1922年至1928年间观察到的快速复苏进行简单外推，而是将复苏缺口建模为……
tldr: 本文通过合成控制、合成双重差分、矩阵补全等一系列要求逐步提高的反事实方法，检验1928年后苏联的高速增长是否必须归因于斯大林模式，其核心方法论创新是构建了一个修正的新经济政策反事实基准，而非简单外推1922至1928年的经济复苏。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates whether the Soviet Union's exceptionally rapid post-1928 growth required a specifically Stalinist explanation, using a sequence of increasingly demanding counterfactual methods (synthetic control, synthetic difference in differences, matrix completion, etc.), with its key methodological contribution being a revised New Economic Policy counterfactual that avoids simply extrapolating the 1922–1928 recovery.
